Extended 2026-11-23: a widened closed set (a schema enum, a request word list) is swept for its NEW words over the test tree's planted «unknown word» cases: `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`' planted unknown request named `monitors`, which the widened enum then admitted, and a sweep keyed on a neighbouring word (`focus-window`) did not find it.

The internal Hyprland seam crate's closed request set grew from 6 to 8: a monitors query and one move-to-workspace dispatch (one Lua element holding only a checked window address and an integer workspace).
The seam still has no product caller: no viola verb places a window, prints anything new, or reaches the human's terminal; no CLI verb, refusal, exit code, IPC method or event was added.
The compositor read deadline stays at 5 s and moved from provisional to settled; a test now times it, and a second test witnesses the read's drain cap on an oversize reply.
The test-only recorder tap gained two verbs (record-monitors, record-move); the move was recorded live once on Hyprland 0.56.2 by the tap's own foot window, and the monitors reply keeps numbers and booleans only.
The recorded Hyprland fixture set grew from 7 to 9 files, the fixture schema's request enum from 6 to 8 words; CI green 7/7, no capability claimed.

decision/time-bounds-never-on-human: the settled 5 s compositor read deadline falls on no human input; a picker should confirm the row stays true and that no row needs the bound until a product caller exists.

body_fields.rule: The Hyprland seam's move-to-workspace dispatch crosses to the directly spawned hyprctl child as one argv element into which only a checked window address and an i32 workspace enter, never reply or user text.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds a dispatch whose argv carries values to hyprctl, and the closed shape of that crossing, resting on the overseer's delegated word, binds every later caller of the seam.

body_fields.name: Recorded Hyprland replies keep numbers as host facts
body_fields.rule: A recorded Hyprland reply keeps its numbers and booleans (monitor ids, sizes, positions, scale, focus, active workspace) and no string; the kept numbers are accepted as host facts, the recorder's allowlist governing strings only.
body_fields.because: The new recorded monitors reply commits host numbers that no standing row allows or forbids, and their acceptance, on the delegate's R3 allowance, binds later recordings.

body_fields.name: Hyprland recorder moves only its own terminal's window
body_fields.rule: The test-only Hyprland recorder's move acts only on the window of a terminal it spawned itself, ends and reaps that terminal after the move, and refuses with no-terminal-window when no window of its own terminal appears.
body_fields.because: The recorder gains a verb that acts on a live desktop window, and its bound to a window of its own making is the rule that keeps it off the user's windows.

body_fields.value: Every hygiene violation class is proven red by a planted input; a planted unknown-word case names a word outside the closed set, and when the set widens every planted case naming a new word moves to a word still outside it.
body_fields.because: Widening the Hyprland request enum turned the planted unknown-request case valid until it was re-pointed to a word still outside the set, so the planted-case rule must say that a planted unknown word follows the set it tests.

body_fields.name: Recorded window move only on the tap's own terminal
body_fields.rule: A recorded dispatch that moves a window acts only on a terminal the recording tap itself started, ends that terminal and confirms its window is gone; it never places a host window it did not open.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds the first recorded Hyprland dispatch that moves a window, recorded only against the tap's own terminal under the directive's host rule, and no test-plan row says what a moving recording may act on.

body_fields.name: Hyprland monitors and dispatch recordings keep no host text
body_fields.rule: A recorded Hyprland monitors reply keeps numbers and booleans alone and no string, and a recorded dispatch reply is kept only as its success text; the fixture hygiene walk rejects a planted monitors string and a planted non-success dispatch reply.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds the monitors query and the move dispatch to the recorded set with their keep-list entries and planted hygiene cases, and the standing walk row names the per-request keep-list only in general and has no room left under its bound.

body:
The Hyprland seam's closed request set grew from 6 to 8: a monitors query and one move-to-workspace dispatch, the move crossing to hyprctl as ONE argv element holding only a checked window address and an i32 workspace.
A monitors reply is read into a closed Monitor type with no text field (id, size, position, focused, active workspace), under the MAX_FRAME cap and serde's default depth; the reply's text is dropped at the parse.
The hyprctl read deadline was settled at its unchanged 5 s (no longer provisional), timed by a test, and the drain past the cap was witnessed by a test that keeps one byte past MAX_FRAME and reads oversize.
The test-only Hyprland recorder tap gained two verbs, record-monitors and record-move; its string keep-list keeps no monitors string and a move reply only as its success text; two scrubbed fixtures were recorded on the host (Hyprland 0.56.2), the move once on the operator's own word.
The seam still has no product caller: no viola verb places a window; no IPC method, socket, env var, dependency or crate was added and nothing was retired.

the recorder tap's rehearsal tests over planted hyprctl and terminal stubs

the Hyprland seam contract - recorded replies replayed through the fake and parsed into their types
the recorded fixture hygiene walk - planted unclean or unknown-request Hyprland fixtures refused
the Hyprland fixture schema - its closed request word enum
the hyprctl JSON parser fuzz target, a parser surface in fuzz scope
a recorded, scrubbed Hyprland monitors reply fixture - numbers and booleans only, every string the placeholder

Expected amendment.

decision/bounded-readers-census and decision/bounded-external-readers: the hyprctl reply Boundary row's witness moved to read_of_a_reply_twice_the_cap_keeps_one_byte_past_it_and_is_oversize, and its types text now also names Monitor; needle and cap unchanged.

decision/max-frame-cap, decision/max-frame-shared-cap and decision/reads-capped-at-max-frame: a new parser (parse_monitors) refuses one byte past MAX_FRAME as oversize, and the drain of the hyprctl child keeps MAX_FRAME plus one byte while the child writes (drain-cap control).

decision/child-output-bounded and decision/child-output-tolerant: the hyprctl child's output for two new requests is read bounded and tolerantly (a key of another type read as absent, an element without an id stepped over, a non-array reply malformed).

decision/json-default-depth-limit and decision/serde-json-bounded-depth: the monitors parse reads at serde's default depth - a new reader under the rule, no exception.

decision/fixture-recording-scrubbed, decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal, decision/fixture-hygiene and decision/fixtures-reviewed-before-commit: two new recorded Hyprland fixtures, each scrubbed by the keep-list, the monitors one read back by hand before landing; the hygiene walk's planted unknown request word moved from monitors to exec since the schema now admits monitors.
decision/closed-types-for-protocol-fields and decision/upstream-text-is-content: the move dispatch argv admits only a closed Address and an i32; no reply text or user text enters the hyprctl argv.
decision/new-env-read-needs-log-entry: the seam gained two requests and reads no new env var; its instrumentation is the standing hyprctl-probe spawn pair and parse-rejected log entry.

decision/release-build-no-test-binaries and decision/release-build-without-test-features: the test-only recorder tap gained the record-monitors and record-move verbs; it stays a test-only binary outside the release build.
decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty (by analogy): the tap's record-move moves only the window of a terminal it spawned itself, then ends and reaps that terminal and checks its window gone.

A recorded Hyprland monitors reply keeps its numbers and booleans (monitor ids, sizes, positions, scale, focus, active workspace) and no string; kept numbers are accepted as host facts, since the recorder allowlist governs strings only.

The test-only Hyprland recorder's move acts only on the window of a terminal it spawned itself, ends and reaps that terminal after the move, and refuses with no-terminal-window when no window of its own terminal appears.

Time-faked-through-seams, no test-owned real time and no sleep synchronisation: a unit test waits out the real 5 s compositor read deadline (about 5.01 s). The tap's record-move also polls the compositor with a bounded loop.
Closed enums change only by decision: the seam's closed request set and the schema's request enum each widened by two words on the operator's and overseer's decisions.
Recorded fixtures replayed and fake matches recordings byte for byte, and fixture drift compared byte for byte: the replay set now holds 9 Hyprland files, including the first recorded dispatch.
Test-only E2E crate and single test-only crate rows: the test-only tap binary in that crate gained two verbs and a terminal it spawns and ends.
External processes are real stub executables: the tap's rehearsals plant stub hyprctl and stub terminal scripts that answer the move.

No human-in-loop verification, live verify never in CI, and live readings recorded as readings: the two recordings were fired live once on a host by the operator pass and are never re-fired by a test. CI only replays them.
Mocks only at product seams: the Hyprland seam is the product seam its fake replays. It still has no product caller.
No unbounded JSON depth: the monitors parse reads at serde's default depth after a MAX_FRAME length check.
